Sam Rodriguez: Quick Q — provisioning a GPU nodepool for inference-training. Want to prefer spot for cost but auto-fallback to reserved when spots are gone. Our TF currently sets label `spot_preferred = "true"` on the node pool. Is a label alone enough to steer scheduling, or do we need taints/affinity? Also how do you recommend doing capacity reservations — separate reserved pool vs autoscaler policy fallback?

Elena Vasquez: Label alone won't change where pods land. You need either taints+tolerations or nodeAffinity + pod priority. Our pattern: spot pool = tainted (`spot=true:NoSchedule`) & lower pod priority class, reserved pool = no taint or higher priority. Autoscaler scales both but we treat reserved as guaranteed capacity.

Michael Tan: For TF snippet, we set `preemptible = true` on the spot pool and add `taints = [{ key = "spot", value = "true", effect = "NO_SCHEDULE" }]`. Then pods that can tolerate will land there. Example (pseudo-TF):
```hcl
resource "node_pool" "gpu_spot" {
  name        = "gpu-spot"
  machine_type = "p4d.24xlarge"
  preemptible = true
  labels = {
    spot_preferred = "true"
  }
  taints = [{ key = "spot", value = "true", effect = "NO_SCHEDULE" }]
}
```

Elena Vasquez: Also add a small node affinity on the pod spec instead of relying only on labels if you want stronger preference: `nodeAffinity.preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` with weight for spot nodes. But if you need automatic fallback when spot gone, the real lever is pod priorities + reserved pool with higher priority.

Jia Chen: FYI make sure the nodepool IAM role includes volume and S3 access for model downloads + metrics. We had a wiring issue last week where the reserved pool role didn't have the S3 policy so model pull failed when pods landed on reserved. Doc: https://internal.redwood/ops/secret-wiring (quick link).

infra-bot: deploy-bot: plan for `cluster/gpu-spot` nodepool provisioning diff OK — no destructive changes; awaiting PR merge.

Sam Rodriguez: Cool. I'll open a PR that creates two nodepools: `gpu-spot` (tainted + preemptible) and `gpu-reserved` (no taint). I'll add a small canary deployment with toleration to validate scheduling. Also want to add graceful node draining before termination — autoscaler config supports `gracefulDrainingSeconds = 300` right?

Michael Tan: Yep add `gracefulDrainingSeconds = 300` (or 5min) in your autoscaler policy. Also set `max_pods_eviction=2` to avoid simultaneous eviction storms.

Elena Vasquez: :thumbsup: For testing, create a tiny pod with toleration & `priorityClass: spot-low` so it prefers spot but will fall back to reserved. Once canary OK, roll real workloads.

Sam Rodriguez: Will do. PR ETA EOD PST. Ping me for review pls. Thanks!
